events.description: US embassy bombings, the biggest al-Qaeda attack before 9/11. EIJ operatives laid the groundwork, with Hezbollah and Iran assistance per the hosts.
Mumbai attacks by Lashkar-e-Taiba; Headley did surveillance, later also for al-Qaeda plots.
TTP controls Buner, about 60 miles from Islamabad, prompting the Pakistani military offensive. Also Gen. Flynn's remark that the Haqqanis are a negotiable criminal group.
Osama bin Laden killed in Abbottabad; Hafiz Saeed called him a martyr.
Al-Qaeda kidnapped an Iranian diplomat; he was reportedly exchanged for al-Qaeda detainees in Iran. Three of them left and were killed in Syria; Saif al-Adel and Abu Muhammad al-Masri stayed.
US Treasury designated three senior al-Qaeda terrorists in Iran, including Abu Hamza al-Khalidi as head of al-Qaeda's military committee.
Hafiz Saeed convicted on terrorism financing charges, but not seriously jailed.
US-Taliban deal signed; US to close five bases and withdraw 4,000 troops within 135 days.
Gen. McKenzie says Zawahiri is in eastern Afghanistan.
Pakistan asked the UN to free up funds for about 50 known jihadists, including Hafiz Saeed.
US and Afghan forces raided two massive al-Qaeda training camps in Shorabak, Kandahar, forcing revision of the 50-100 estimate.
Obama administration designations of three senior al-Qaeda figures in Iran, including Abu Hamza al-Khalidi as head of the military committee
Abu al-Khayr al-Masri, Zawahiri's top deputy, killed in a US drone strike in Syria
Asim Umar, AQIS emir, killed in Helmand along with his courier to Zawahiri
AQAP-linked attack at Naval Air Station Pensacola by Saudi second lieutenant Mohammed al-Shamrani
Qasim al-Raymi, AQAP emir, recently killed in Yemen
Abdelmalek Droukdel killed in a French-led operation with US assistance
State Department country reports on terrorism say al-Qaeda's facilitation network in Iran is still operating
Baghdadi declares himself caliph in a video; hosts joke about the watch he wore.

key_claims: Al-Qaeda in 2020 is alive but misunderstood: its emir Zawahiri is in eastern Afghanistan per CENTCOM and the UN says AQ operates clandestinely in at least 12 Afghan provinces.

Al-Qaeda survived the war through its alliance with the Haqqani Network, whose founder Jalaluddin Haqqani was one of bin Laden's earliest benefactors and whose current leader Sirajuddin Haqqani is a Taliban deputy emir.

Al-Qaeda's senior leadership is partly based in Iran under a standing arrangement: Saif al-Adel and Abu Muhammad al-Masri live there and sit on the succession chain, and Abu Hamza al-Khalidi ran AQ's military committee from Iran.

Al-Qaeda's regional branches (AQAP, AQIM, Shabaab, AQIS, Hurras al-Din) remain loyal to Zawahiri and their emirs double as AQ deputies/general managers, so the core-vs-branch distinction is misleading.
Pakistan's state is 'in bed' with Lashkar-e-Taiba and tolerates Hafiz Saeed; parts of LeT have long been wedded to al-Qaeda.
Successive leadership losses (Abu al-Khayr al-Masri, Wuhayshi, Droukdel, Asim Umar, Raymi) have not collapsed the organization because replacements were pre-positioned.
